description_good: README.md describes what Lotus Share does: share files and messages between devices on the same local network, no Internet or account: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/README.md
interact: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md explain how to get the source and binaries, report bugs (issue forms), request features and contribute: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the pull request process (section 'Contributing in English'): https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements: required CI checks, tests for every change, Conventional Commits, Apache-2.0-compatible dependencies: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
documentation_basics: README.md covers installation (Scoop, Homebrew, APT/RPM, installers), verification and development; docs/KIEN-TRUC-KY-THUAT.md covers the architecture: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface: The app is a GUI; the network protocol it exposes (port 53420, multicast group, /api/lotus/v2/ endpoints) is documented in docs/vi/KHAM-PHA-THIET-BI.md, and the CLI documents its options with --help: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/docs/vi/KHAM-PHA-THIET-BI.md
sites_https: Project site https://lotus.tsudev.com (HSTS) and the GitHub repository/releases are HTTPS only.
discussion: GitHub Issues and Discussions are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/issues
english: English documentation and bug reports are accepted: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/README.md
maintained: Actively maintained: releases on 10-13/11/2026 and regular commits: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/commits/main
repo_track: Git tracks every change with author and date.
repo_interim: Work in progress is pushed to branches and pull requests between releases.
version_unique: Each release has a unique version and git tag: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/tags
version_semver: SemVer of the product plus a release counter (2.0.0-lotus.7); the ecosystem moves to calendar versions YY.M.DDNN from the next release.
release_notes: CHANGELOG.md summarises every release in human-readable form (also shown in the app and on the website): https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns: CHANGELOG.md lists the RUSTSEC identifiers fixed in each release (1.18.2-lotus.2, 1.18.2-lotus.3): https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
report_process: Bug reports use GitHub Issues with issue forms: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/issues/new/choose
report_responses: No external bug report has been filed so far; the maintainer reads every issue and acknowledges reports within days.
enhancement_responses: No external enhancement request has been filed so far; the feature request form routes them to the maintainer, who answers each one.
report_archive: GitHub Issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process: SECURITY.md (Vietnamese + English summary) explains how to report vulnerabilities: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response: No vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to a reply within 72 hours.
build: The release workflow builds every platform from source on GitHub Actions (flutter build + cargo): https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-lotus.yml
build_common_tools: Flutter/Dart (pub), Rust (cargo), Gradle, Inno Setup, appimage-builder.
build_floss_tools: Flutter, Dart, Rust, cargo, Gradle, Inno Setup and appimage-builder are FLOSS (Xcode is only needed for the optional macOS build).
test: Automated tests: Dart tests in app/test and Rust unit + integration tests in packages/core (TLS pinning, PIN brute-force limits, protocol constants, discovery): https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/tree/main/packages/core/tests
test_invocation: flutter test and cargo test --features full (documented in AGENTS.md section B.2 and CONTRIBUTING.md).
test_most: Tests cover the security-critical core (TLS certificate pinning, PIN checks, request limits, upload/download sessions, discovery) and the app's settings, persistence migration, i18n and legal assets.
test_continuous_integration: GitHub Actions runs format, analyze, clippy and all tests on every push and pull request; they are required checks for main: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy: CONTRIBUTING.md requires automated tests for every new feature or bug fix: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added: Recent changes added tests with the code, e.g. packages/core/tests/protocol_constants.rs with the multicast fix (PR #42) and the PIN hardening tests: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/pull/42
tests_documented_added: The test policy is written in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings: flutter analyze (Dart analyzer with lints) and cargo clippy run in CI: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
warnings_fixed: CI fails on any flutter analyze issue (zero issues on main); clippy findings in the Rust core are reviewed and fixed in pull requests.
warnings_strict: The Dart analyzer runs with the flutter_lints rule set and fails the build on any issue; clippy runs on all targets with every feature enabled.
know_secure_design: docs/vi/KIEN-TRUC-BAO-MAT.md documents the threat model and defences (per-device TLS certificates identified by SHA-256 fingerprint, mutual TLS, PIN brute-force limits, no proxy/redirects): https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/docs/vi/KIEN-TRUC-BAO-MAT.md
know_common_errors: The security architecture lists the common errors for a LAN transfer tool (device impersonation via spoofed discovery packets, PIN guessing including IPv6 address rotation, connection floods, proxy/redirect abuse, quick-save from strangers) and the mitigation for each: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/docs/vi/KIEN-TRUC-BAO-MAT.md
crypto_published: Uses only published, reviewed algorithms: TLS 1.2/1.3 via rustls, RSA-2048 keys, RSA-PSS with SHA-256, SHA-256 fingerprints, Ed25519.
crypto_call: All cryptography is delegated to established libraries (rustls, ring, RustCrypto rsa/sha2/ed25519-dalek, rcgen); the project implements no primitive itself.
crypto_keylength: Device keys are RSA 2048-bit (NIST minimum through 2030); TLS uses rustls' default cipher suites.
crypto_working: No broken algorithms: rustls does not offer RC4, 3DES, MD5 or SHA-1 cipher suites; fingerprints use SHA-256.
crypto_weaknesses: No SHA-1/MD5 or other algorithms with known serious weaknesses are used for security.
crypto_pfs: rustls only negotiates ECDHE key exchange (TLS 1.2) or TLS 1.3, both providing perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_password_storage: The software has no user accounts and stores no passwords for authenticating external users. The optional receive PIN is a local setting compared in constant time with attempt limits.
crypto_random: Keys, PINs, session IDs and tokens come from the OS CSPRNG (OsRng/getrandom, Random.secure); PIN generation fails closed if no CSPRNG is available.
delivery_mitm: Releases are downloaded over HTTPS from GitHub; SHA256SUMS.txt is signed with Sigstore and each file has a GitHub artifact attestation (gh attestation verify); APKs are signed with a pinned certificate.
delivery_unsigned: Hashes are published in a Sigstore-signed SHA256SUMS.txt over HTTPS, never over plain HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days: No unpatched vulnerability of medium or higher severity affects the software: 0 open Dependabot alerts; the OSV scan runs on every change and only accepts documented, time-limited exceptions. RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (rsa, Marvin timing attack, no fixed release) does not apply: rsa is only used to generate keys and verify RSA-PSS signatures with public keys; TLS private-key operations use ring. RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (crypto-bigint) is only reachable through the WebRTC transport, which is disabled in the app: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/tools/osv_scan.py
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed: No critical vulnerability has been reported; Dependabot and the OSV scan keep dependencies patched (e.g. RUSTSEC-2026-0486 fixed the day it was published).
no_leaked_credentials: gitleaks scans the full history on every push and pull request; signing keys live outside the repository: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml
static_analysis: CodeQL (Rust, Actions), cargo clippy and the Dart analyzer analyse every change: https://github.com/tsudev-org/lotus-share/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities: CodeQL security queries look for common vulnerabilities (certificate validation, hard-coded credentials, injection, workflow permissions).
static_analysis_fixed: All medium and higher CodeQL findings were fixed or triaged with a written reason; there are no open code scanning alerts.
static_analysis_often: Static analysis runs on every push and pull request.
dynamic_analysis: Integration tests run real HTTPS servers and clients against each other (TLS pinning, malformed and oversized requests, connection floods in accept_resilience.rs) on every change.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe: The core is Rust and the app is Dart (memory-safe). The only unsafe blocks wrap OS file descriptors (File::from_raw_fd on Android); no sanitizer run is configured yet.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions: Tests run debug builds with assertions enabled (cargo test, flutter test).
dynamic_analysis_fixed: No medium or higher severity issue found by dynamic analysis remains unfixed.
